title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — Cap. 2 §17: common/immediate prior to each person's existence and corruption
pass_a_gloss: He presses Garrigues's Cap. 2 §17 wording: that common/immediate imputation is later than Adam's first actual transgression yet prior to each descendant's personal existence and the corruption that descends by generation—because from the beginning all were commonly in Adam, not already as separate persons distant from him.
pass_b_english: And a little later he says: "But with human nature existing in that principal individual, men can also be said to have existed commonly in him." Existed, that is, distant and separate from Adam's person? I do not think anyone will say that. And Cap. 2 §17: "That common or immediate [imputation]," he says, "just as it was later than Adam's first actual transgression, so it was prior to the personal existence of each man born of Adam, and so also to that corruption which descends into individuals by natural generation, insofar as from the beginning all flowed commonly in Adam."
source_text: Et paulo post inquit: Existente autem humana natura in individuo illo principiali, in illo etiam dici possunt homines communiter extitisse. Extiteruntne scilicet a persona Adami distantes & separati? Non arbitror quenquam hoc dicturum. Et Cap. 2. §. xvii. Communis, inquit, illa sive immediata, quemadmodum posterior fuit prima actuali Adami transgressione, ita prior fuit personali cuiuscumque hominis ex Adamo prognati existentia atque adeo etiam corruptione illa quae in singulos naturali generatione descendit, quatenus ab initio resuerunt omnes communiter in Adamo.
